newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: THREE FLORIDA WOMEN NABBED FOR THEFT IN CAYMANS.
newsitem.headline: THREE FLORIDA WOMEN NABBED FOR THEFT IN CAYMANS.

text.p: Three women, including an assistant school principal and a sheriff's department officer, were convicted of stealing a purse while on vacation in the Cayman Islands, officials said Wednesday.

Joyce Jones, 38, Clavelia Brinson, 50, and Angeleeta Todd, 42, of Jacksonville, Florida, were each fined $625 and ordered deported to the United States by George Town magistrate Peter Jackson on Monday.
They had pleaded guilty. They faced a two-month jail sentence if they are unable to pay the fine.
The three women said they arrived in Grand Cayman last Friday on board the cruise ship Sea Breeze.

Todd admitted stealing a purse on a counter at a George Town store that contained $4,351 in cash. The other two women were convicted of handling stolen goods after they both admitted taking some of the money.
At first they denied theft, saying they had found the purse and were looking for the owner. But some of the money was missing and police later found the woman had it.
They spent the weekend in a police cell.

Jones gave her occupation as a correctional officer with the Jacksonville sheriff's office, Brinson said she was assistant principal at a Jacksonville high school, and Todd said she was a shipping clerk.
